prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien

(2 PRs)

prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same defect in `_handle_reconnection`: when SSE reconnection exceeds MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the original code just logged at debug level and returned with no error surfaced anywhere, leaving the caller that was waiting on that request hanging indefinitely. #2395 sends a properly-correlated JSONRPCError (using the pending request's own id) back through read_stream_writer so only that specific request fails while the rest of the session keeps running. #3098 instead adds an `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull a `StreamableHTTPError` out of an anyio ExceptionGroup, implying the failure is raised and propagated up through the TaskGroup instead - a coarser-grained approach that would tear down the whole client/session on a single stream's reconnection failure rather than failing just the affected request. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same defect in `_handle_reconnection`: when SSE reconnection exceeds MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the original code just logged at debug level and returned with no error surfaced anywhere, leaving the caller that was waiting on that request hanging indefinitely. #2395 sends a properly-correlated JSONRPCError (using the pending request's own id) back through read_stream_writer so only that specific request fails while the rest of the session keeps running. #3098 instead adds an `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull a `StreamableHTTPError` out of an anyio ExceptionGroup, implying the failure is raised and propagated up through the TaskGroup instead - a coarser-grained approach that would tear down the whole client/session on a single stream's reconnection failure rather than failing just the affected request. (2 PRs)

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthContext.oauth_metadata (authorization server metadata, including the token endpoint) is only ever kept in memory. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2492 addresses this by adding new optional `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` methods to the `TokenStorage` protocol, defaulting to no-ops — the fix only takes effect for storage backends that are updated to implement them, so existing/third-party storage implementations see no benefit until they opt in. #3263 fixes it at the provider level instead: it rediscovers AS metadata inline before a cold-start refresh (guarded by a new `eager_discovery_attempted` flag so a metadata-less server isn't re-probed on every in-process refresh) and adds an issuer-binding check on the rediscovered metadata that #2492 has no equivalent for. #3263 works immediately for every existing storage implementation without requiring any protocol changes, and adds a security check #2492 lacks.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a quote/escape-aware comma splitter for the header, but #3041's version explicitly detects scheme boundaries within the split segments (_extract_bearer_auth_params walks segments and stops collecting once a new scheme token like 'DPoP' appears), so it correctly isolates the Bearer challenge's params when a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. 'Bearer ..., DPoP ...'). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips the text before the first space once and then treats everything after as one flat, undifferentiated param list, so it would merge a second challenge's scheme name and params into the Bearer param list instead of excluding them.
